faqs.q: How much does a Norwegian Lundehund cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Norwegian Lundehund puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Norwegian Lundehund, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Norwegian Lundehund cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Norwegian Lundehund are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows. The dense undercoat requires a dedicated undercoat rake, not just a surface slicker brush. Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Norwegian Lundehunds shed a lot?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds have seasonal shedding — manageable with a consistent brushing routine.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Norwegian Lundehund need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Norwegian Lundehund is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Norwegian Lundehunds that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Norwegian Lundehunds easy to train?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Norwegian Lundehunds. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Most Norwegian Lundehunds learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Norwegian Lundehunds commonly have?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds are most commonly associated with brachycephalic airway issues. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Norwegian Lundehunds live?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds have an average lifespan of 12–15 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Norwegian Lundehunds prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Norwegian Lundehund puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Norwegian Lundehund puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Norwegian Lundehund-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Norwegian Lundehunds good with kids?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds can be protective and may be cautious around unfamiliar children. Early socialisation with children from puppyhood significantly improves tolerance. Always supervise interactions between dogs and young children.

faqs.q: Do Norwegian Lundehunds get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Norwegian Lundehunds bark a lot?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Norwegian Lundehunds good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Norwegian Lundehund need per day?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Norwegian Lundehunds good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Norwegian Lundehunds make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Norwegian Lundehund doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Norwegian Lundehunds often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Norwegian Lundehund be off-lead?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: A Norwegian Lundehund needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Adult Norwegian Lundehunds should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Norwegian Lundehunds benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Norwegian Lundehund from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Norwegian Lundehunds can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Norwegian Lundehund a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Norwegian Lundehunds good family dogs?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds can be excellent family dogs for active households. They thrive with children who can match their energy level. A calm household with limited exercise may not suit this breed's temperament.

faqs.q: Do Norwegian Lundehunds do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Norwegian Lundehunds form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Norwegian Lundehund?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Norwegian Lundehund — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
